sections.overview: This emballonurid bat occurs across parts of sub-Saharan Africa, Arabia and Madagascar.
sections.identification: It is a small, dark-brown bat with paler underparts; published descriptions give a mass around 10–12 g.
sections.habitat: It roosts in illuminated caves, rocky crevices and sometimes house cellars, often near coasts or lakes.
sections.diet: It is insectivorous; reported prey includes beetles and moths, with feeding activity higher in the rainy season.
sections.behavior: On mainland Africa it may form large roosting colonies numbering in the thousands.
sections.reproduction: Species-specific breeding details were not available in the Red List account consulted.
sections.ecology: The genus Coleura also includes the Seychelles Sheath-tailed Bat, C. seychellensis, a much more restricted island relative.
sections.conservation: The IUCN assessment published in 2017 lists C. afra as Least Concern, while noting that population trend is unknown.
